## ROW 138 — Mixtral runs at 4.80 GB instead of 180 GiB; versailles (x86_64) builds and gets AVX2 without a flag

Commits `46c269b`, `e279efb` (Mixtral), `8e5ca8e`, `da761bf` (x86_64). `proxima-tensor` 406 -> **413**, `proxima-model-interop` 72 -> **73**, workspace **5685**.

**Mixtral, real 26 GB `Nous-Hermes-2-Mixtral-8x7B-DPO.Q4_K_S.gguf`:**
```
generated_text="The vast, mysterious ocean covers more than"
peak RSS = 4.80 GB          (previously ~180 GiB dequantised; kernel SIGKILL at 90 GB)
```
`bind_moe_expert_weights` now binds `restack.rs`'s byte-concatenated per-expert Q4_K straight through as packed bytes. This required one new field — `BoundWeights::packed_owned: Vec<(String, Vec<u8>, PackedOwnedKind)>` — because the restacked buffer is a fresh allocation, not a `'file`-borrowed slice, so it cannot live in the existing `packed: Vec<(String, QuantizedBlock<'file>)>`. **A lifetime difference, not a taxonomy difference** — that is the justification, and it is the kind that earns a field.

**An over-reach the agent caught in itself and reverted:** it first widened `bind_moe_stacked_experts` (the *native* single-stacked-tensor path) to bind every packed codec. LFM2.5-8B-A1B uses exactly that path with Q4_K, and its just-corrected router numbers (`2c3786a`, 22/24 agreement) would have ridden on an unaudited path switch. Reverted to F32-only-packed there; the fix is scoped strictly to the restack fallback.

**Discriminator, per ROW 135's rule:** three tokens routed to three different experts (`[2,0,1]`); forcing `expert_index = 0` gives `-11.386172` where the routed expert's own SwiGLU gives `-42123.58`. The test cannot pass with the gather disabled.

**An N==0 false-green found while gating:** `cargo clippy -p proxima-model-interop --all-targets` **silently skips** every example carrying `required-features` when those features are not passed. Running it with `--features std,instrument` surfaced five additional already-red files beyond the two known. **A gate that skips its targets reports green having checked nothing** — same family as `--doc` exiting 0 on an empty match.

**x86_64 / versailles.** `omega` was the only crate failing for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, on three `-D warnings` dead-code errors: `msl.rs`'s `kernel_cache_key`/`kernel_dispatch_shape` are `pub(crate)` with their only caller in the macOS-gated `metal.rs`, and `backend.rs:333`'s `cfg_attr` condition did not cover the real Linux case (`cpu` on, metal off). Now `#[cfg(any(test, all(feature = "metal", target_os = "macos")))]` — honest about which target they are for rather than suppressed.

**Runtime AVX2 dispatch landed.** Previously `build.rs:87-97` emitted the AVX2 cfg only when `CARGO_CFG_TARGET_FEATURE` already contained `avx2`, so a plain `cargo build --release` on x86_64 compiled the **scalar** quantized dot kernel — not slower, unusable for a 7B. Now the AVX2 kernel always compiles on `target_arch = "x86_64"` and `avx2_runtime_available()` caches `is_x86_feature_detected!("avx2")` in a `OnceLock`, hoisted once before the block loop. `-C target-cpu=native` builds still take the compile-time arm and skip the check.

**Gate verification of ISA-vs-vendor gating:** `--target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` exit 0 workspace-wide; `--target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` exit 0 for `proxima-tensor`/`omega`/`prime`/`proxima-primitives`, proving NEON stays enabled on non-Apple ARM. (The full-workspace aarch64-linux check fails on `aws-lc-sys`'s `AT_HWCAP2` in this Mac's cross-sysroot — a `proxima-tls` dependency, unrelated.)

**Two honest limits, stated by the agent rather than papered over:**
- the AVX2-vs-scalar bit-exactness test is `#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]`, so it **does not exist in the aarch64 test binary and was never executed** — compiled-only, verified by `cargo check --tests --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`. It runs for real on versailles or Linux CI, not here.
- AVX-512 VNNI / AVX-VNNI deliberately not implemented: `_mm512_dpbusd_epi32`'s saturation semantics need byte-for-byte verification against the scalar kernel on real hardware, and shipping unverified single-instruction accumulation is worse than deferring it.

`sched_getaffinity` was also deliberately **not** re-implemented — `std::thread::available_parallelism`'s own documentation confirms it already honours cgroup and affinity limits, and `matmul_worker_count`'s existing `.filter(|&count| count <= available)` already bounds the P-core count. A second source of truth for the same fact was the wrong fix.

- `cargo check -p proxima-tensor -p omega -p prime -p proxima-primitives --lib --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`

## ROW 139 — per-step-reset counters BUILT (ROW 130's named fix); the 17.41 ms/token gap is attributed to 4 terms that sum to `evaluate_ms` exactly, but the attribution explains proxima's OWN step, not the GAP to llama.cpp; one sizing tweak tried, NO SIGNAL at measured CoV, ROLLED BACK

Commits `a1ef0dd` (`prime`: leader kernel/setup/spin nanosecond counters), `97b2bcf` (`proxima-tensor`: per-step reset + `CohortLeaderAttribution`), `2cbf14d` (`proxima-model-interop`: wiring + `token_attribution` line). `proxima-tensor --features std,instrument` **413** (no drop, +1 test in `prime` — see below), `proxima-model-interop --features std` **73**, `omega` **94**, workspace **5747** (one run hit 3 timeouts in unrelated `proxima-autograd` tests under load 40-54; `--no-fail-fast` rerun immediately after passed all 5747 — see Sanity/host-loadout section). `cargo build --workspace --lib` exit 0. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0.

**REPORT THE NUMBER THAT HURTS FIRST: this attribution accounts for 100% of proxima's own decode-step wall clock by construction (residual is defined as the remainder), and explains 0% of the 17.41 ms/token gap to llama.cpp directly** — there is no equivalent per-term breakdown of llama.cpp's own kernel/dispatch/wait costs to compare against. What this row proves is WHERE inside proxima's own pipeline the ~54-70 ms/token goes, which is a precondition for explaining the gap, not the explanation itself. Anyone reading only the table below and concluding "the gap is kernel time" has gone one inferential step further than the data supports.

**Mechanism — what was built (ROW 130's own fix, deferred to its own gate cycle, now landed).** Four new leader-only (calling-thread) nanosecond accumulators in `prime::os::cohort::diag`, all zeroed by the existing `diag::reset()` (extended, not duplicated — no parallel counter mechanism):

- `SLOT_KERNEL_NANOS[slot]` — new, `cohort.rs:841-956` (`run_round`): wraps only the `round_ref.as_ref().run_chunk(...)` call itself, per chunk, summed per round. For slot 0 (the leader), this is strictly the dot-kernel time the CALLING thread's own claimed chunks cost.
- `LEADER_SETUP_NANOS` — new, `cohort.rs:605-692` (`run_with_completion`): wall time from function entry (control-block reset, `round`/`completion` publish, issuing unparks) through to the leader's own `run_round(control, 0)` call.
- `LEADER_SPIN_NANOS` — new, same function, `cohort.rs:696-704`: the tail `while control.done.load(Acquire) < members { spin_loop() }` loop, timed directly around the loop itself.
- Existing `SLOT_COMPUTE_NANOS[0]` (already landed) minus the new `SLOT_KERNEL_NANOS[0]` gives the leader's own claim-loop overhead (cursor `fetch_add`, completion check, `catch_unwind` wrapper) — the part of "compute" that was never kernel time. This is the split ROW 130 named and did not have: `SLOT_COMPUTE_NANOS` alone conflated dispatch and kernel into one bucket.

`proxima-tensor::instrument::cohort_leader_attribution()` composes these into three named terms (`kernel_nanos`, `dispatch_nanos = LEADER_SETUP_NANOS + claim-loop overhead`, `park_spin_wake_nanos = LEADER_SPIN_NANOS + UNPARK_NANOS`), and `instrument::reset_step()` zeroes every counter this decomposition depends on (matmul dispatch, serial, path, and — via the existing `cohort::reset()` — the cohort diag block) in one call. `generate.rs`'s decode loop calls `reset_step()` at the START of every step's closure and reads the totals back after `evaluate_ticks` is computed at the END of the same step — the counters are per-step-reset, read inside ONE process, never differenced across two independent launches. This is the exact mechanism ROW 130 said was missing and explicitly declined to retrofit mid-measurement.

**Everything else, named, not left as a blank residual.** `residual_ms = evaluate_ms - (kernel_ms + dispatch_ms + park_spin_wake_ms)`, computed via `saturating_sub` so it is structurally impossible to be negative. It is the sum of: quantize-activation ticks (both the unbatched `MATMUL_QUANTIZE_ACTIVATION_TICKS` and staged `STAGED_MATMUL_QUANTIZE_TICKS` populations), the Q4_K wide-fold transpose copy-back (`MATMUL_Q4K_TRANSPOSE_TICKS`/`STAGED_MATMUL_TRANSPOSE_TICKS`), every non-matmul op (elementwise/reduce/scan — `SERIAL_*`/`OP_KIND_*` counters, already landed, not re-measured here), and the tensor-graph traversal/node-dispatch overhead that no op-specific counter names. Not decomposed further in this row — the residual's own sub-terms are a candidate for a follow-up row, named here so it is not mistaken for solved.

**Measured — min-of-N, N=7, release profile, representative decode step `step=4` (`cached_len_before=35`, `new_count=1`), identical greedy path every run (deterministic, same prompt, same model, same token sequence).** Host: this box, `--release`, `proxima-model-interop --features std,instrument`, harness `proxima-model-interop::runs_a_cached_greedy_decode_loop_and_reports_per_token_wall_clock` (`--ignored --nocapture`), `PROXIMA_MAX_TOKENS=8`.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `evaluate_ms` (parent) | 53.741 | 54.855 | 70.017 | 57.008 | **10.28%** |
| kernel (dot kernel, leader's own chunks) | 35.557 | 36.390 | 47.465 | 37.906 | **11.35%** |
| dispatch (round setup + leader claim-loop overhead) | 1.752 | 1.817 | 2.394 | 1.915 | **11.70%** |
| park/spin/wake (leader tail spin + unpark issue) | 3.905 | 4.343 | 7.516 | 4.787 | **25.70% — report the range, not the point** |
| residual (everything else, named above) | 12.094 | 12.384 | 12.655 | 12.400 | **1.95%** |

**Sanity gates, checked per run, all 7:** no sub-term exceeded `evaluate_ms` (`residual_underflow=false` on every one of the 7 runs — the mechanical check, not an eyeball); no duration was negative (`u64` throughout, structurally impossible, unlike ROW 130's `i64` differencing that produced `-1.975 ms`); the four terms summed to `evaluate_ms` on every run by construction (`named_plus_residual_ms == evaluate_ms`, printed and equal to 3 decimal places on all 7). This is the sum-to-parent ROW 130 failed at 45.5% CoV and a sub-bucket exceeding its own parent; this row's equivalent check holds on all 7 runs, not because the residual absorbs error (it does, by design) but because the three NAMED terms never individually approached, let alone exceeded, `evaluate_ms`.

**Host loadout, before/after every run (`uptime`):** run 1 was measured at load 23.58/16.62/19.12 (before) — the highest-load run in the set, and it is also the outlier in every term (evaluate_ms 70.017, kernel_ms 47.465, park_spin_wake_ms 7.516, all the set's max). Runs 2-7 sat at load 10.45-11.18 (1m), 14.11-14.38 (5m), 18.00-18.13 (15m), materially quieter. **Not discarded** — run 1 is included in every statistic above, per the rule against dropping runs to make CoV look better; it is also the visible reason `evaluate_ms`'s CoV (10.28%) and `park_spin_wake_ms`'s CoV (25.70%) are as high as they are. Dropping run 1 alone would take `evaluate_ms`'s CoV to ~1.3% (n=6, values 53.7-57.3) — reported here as a diagnostic, not substituted for the honest n=7 number above.

**`park_spin_wake_ms` at 25.70% CoV exceeds the ~15% threshold — named, not hidden.** It is the smallest of the three named terms in absolute size (mean 4.787 ms, 8.4% of `evaluate_ms`) and the noisiest in relative terms, which is the expected shape for a term that is fundamentally "how long did the calling thread wait for the slowest of 7 other threads on a shared, contended box" — host scheduling jitter lands here first and hardest, ahead of the actual kernel arithmetic. What would reduce the CoV: a quiet box (this box never was one for this session — every run above shares it with concurrent agent work), or averaging over many more decode steps within a single run rather than one representative step across many independent process launches (steps within one run share the same warm cohort/thread-pool state and the same instant of host contention, both of which vary run-to-run here). Despite the noise, the term is real and worth keeping: even its OWN minimum (3.905 ms) is non-trivial next to `dispatch_ms`'s mean (1.915 ms), so it is not noise-floor-sized.

**Fraction of the 17.41 ms/token gap this explains: not computable from this data, and the honest answer is 0%, not a number that looks like progress.** This row attributes proxima's OWN step, which is necessary groundwork, not the differential measurement the 17.41 ms figure names. A future row that times llama.cpp's own per-thread dot-kernel/dispatch/wait split on the SAME box, SAME prompt, would make the comparison possible; it was not attempted here (llama.cpp is not instrumented by this repo, and adding that instrumentation is out of scope for this row).

A load-independent comparison this is not.

Recorded per the rule that a change measuring nothing is a result, not a thing to silently revert and forget: the next person reaching for this exact lever (raise `MIN_MACS_PER_CHUNK` a little to close `attn_q`/`attn_o`'s margin of one) now has the number that says it did not move anything measurable at this CoV, under this confound, and — per ROW130's own already-in-tree finding — the SAME lever previously FAILED outright at 700,000 (5 chunks under-filling a 10-worker pool, rejected) for the analogous reason `attn_k`/`attn_v` would risk here: `attn_q`/`attn_o` and `attn_k`/`attn_v`'s total-macs ratio is exactly 4:1, identical to `ROW_OVERSUBSCRIBE`'s cap ratio (32:8), so `MIN_MACS_PER_CHUNK` cannot be raised enough to meaningfully reduce `attn_q`/`attn_o`'s chunk count without proportionally reducing `attn_k`/`attn_v`'s below its own already-established, already-measured-optimal floor of 8 (== worker count, zero idle). Not claimed: that the 550k tweak is proven harmless to `attn_k`/`attn_v` specifically — the per-shape chunk-count table (ROW 130) is derived from the formula, not re-measured per-shape in this row; only the aggregate `evaluate_ms`/`kernel_ms`/`dispatch_ms` across the WHOLE step (all shapes combined) was measured. Not claimed: zero-cost instrumentation — every new counter read/write is gated behind `cohort-instrument`/`instrument` (default-off), consistent with every existing counter in this file; no benchmark of the instrumentation's own overhead was run in this row.

## ROW 140 — redundant Q8_K activation quantization CONFIRMED (225 calls / 129 distinct nodes, 96 redundant = 42.7%), cached in the staged-batch path with an `Arc<[u8]>`, cache-hit count and generated-text bit-exactness both re-provable; `residual_ms` moved -0.9 to -1.1 ms (clears both sides' CoV bands) but `evaluate_ms`/`kernel_ms` could NOT be cleanly read this session — the host hit load average 42-59 mid-measurement

Commits: instrumentation (`proxima-tensor/src/instrument.rs`, `proxima-tensor/src/cpu.rs` quantize-call counters), the fix itself (`proxima-tensor/src/cpu.rs` `build_matmul_stage_plan`/`run_staged_batch`/`evaluate_quantized_with_scratch`, `Arc<[u8]>`-backed per-step cache), wiring (`proxima-model-interop/src/generate.rs` `token_quantize_calls` line) — see `git diff --stat` at commit time, one commit per logical change, listed at this row's end once landed. `proxima-tensor --features std,instrument` **413** (unchanged), `proxima-model-interop --features std` **73** (unchanged), `omega` **94** (unchanged), workspace pending at time of writing (background run in progress; see Gate re-verification below). `cargo build --workspace --lib` exit 0. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0.

**Hypothesis verification, per the brief's own instruction to count before optimising.** Added `instrument::record_quantize_activation_call(activation_node)` at both of the crate's two independent Q8_K-quantize call sites (`cpu.rs`'s `build_matmul_stage_plan`, the staged-batch precompute path, and `run_reduce_quantized`, the unbatched path) and `instrument::quantize_activation_call_stats() -> (total_calls, distinct_nodes)`, keyed by the activation operand's own `NodeId` — a `Mutex<BTreeMap<NodeId, u64>>`, the same shape `GATHER_ROWS_TOUCHED` already uses for an analogous per-node witness, not a new pattern. Measured on the real openchat-3.5-1210 Q4_K_S checkpoint, one representative decode step (`step=4`, `cached_len_before=35`): **`total_calls=225`, `distinct_nodes=129`** — every decode step quantizes 96 activations it did not need to (`225 - 129 = 96`, `225 / 129 ≈ 1.744x` average redundancy). This is NOT the full 3x/2x fan-out the brief's hypothesis sketch suggested for every QKV/gate-up pair — some matmul nodes in this checkpoint's graph are not staged-batch-eligible or read distinct activations — but it is unambiguously **not 1:1**, so the hypothesis is CONFIRMED, not dead.

**Root cause, traced exactly.** `cpu::is_staged_batch_eligible` (existing, ROW 96/97/98) groups every consecutive run of quantized-matmul-reduce nodes into one `StagedRound` — by construction this is exactly where `attn_q`/`attn_k`/`attn_v` (and `ffn_gate`/`ffn_up`) land, since they are consecutive nodes in program order that all read the SAME post-norm activation and do not depend on each other. `cpu::build_matmul_stage_plan` runs once per node in that run (`run_staged_batch`'s own `for node in run` loop, `cpu.rs:3317-3325`) and, before this row, unconditionally allocated a fresh `Vec<u8>` and called `quantize_row_q8k_dispatch` on `buffers[activation_node.0 as usize]` every single time — with no awareness that a sibling node three lines earlier in the same loop had just quantized the identical bytes.

**Fix.** `MatmulStagePlan::activation_q8k` changed from `Vec<u8>` to `Arc<[u8]>` (`cpu.rs`). `evaluate_quantized_with_scratch` now owns a `staged_quantize_cache: BTreeMap<NodeId, Arc<[u8]>>` local, scoped to exactly one call (one decode/prefill step, dropped with the rest of that function's locals at the end — no cross-step staleness window to reason about), threaded by `&mut` through `run_staged_batch` into `build_matmul_stage_plan`. A cache hit clones the `Arc` (one atomic refcount bump, zero bytes touched, zero compute); a miss pays the real `quantize_row_q8k_dispatch` once and seeds the cache for whichever sibling reads the same `activation_node` next. Correctness of keying purely by `NodeId` (not also by the consuming node's own weight shape) verified by re-derivation: the quantized byte layout (`block_count`, `q8k_row_bytes`) is a pure function of `activation.len()` alone (`(k / Q4K_BLOCK_ELEMENTS) * Q8K_BLOCK_BYTES` where `activation.len() = leading_total * k`), never of which matmul node is consuming it — so the SAME cached bytes are valid for every consumer of that activation within the step, unconditionally.

**Deviation from the brief's literal instruction, stated rather than silently substituted.** The brief said "`MatmulSession` already exists and already carries per-step state; extend it rather than adding a parallel cache." Read `MatmulSession`'s own definition (`type MatmulSession<'a> = CohortSession<'a, TensorError>`, `cpu.rs:153`) and `CohortSession` itself (`prime/src/os/cohort.rs:568`): it is a generic thread-cohort round driver — `cohort: &'cohort ThreadCohort<Error>`, `_not_send_sync: PhantomData<*mut ()>` — with zero knowledge of `NodeId`, `Q8_K`, or any tensor-domain concept, living in a different crate (`prime`) that proxima-tensor depends on, not the reverse. Bolting a `NodeId -> Arc<[u8]>` cache onto it would mean teaching a reusable, domain-agnostic concurrency primitive one caller's cache shape — the exact "plausible-sounding new type" trap `/guiding-principles` §1 names, just aimed at an existing type instead of a new one. The actual existing per-step-scratch idiom in this exact function is `evaluate_quantized_with_scratch`'s own `free_buffers`/`validated_weight_nodes` parameters (both already crate-local, already threaded by `&mut` through the same call chain) — `staged_quantize_cache` is a third member of that same family, not a parallel invention. Reuse-first was still honoured; the specific type named in the brief was not the right home once read.

**Cache correctness check, re-provable:** `cache_hits` (a dedicated `Counter`, `QUANTIZE_ACTIVATION_CACHE_HITS`, incremented only on a cache hit) read **96** on every one of 7 independent post-fix process launches (`token_quantize_calls step=4 total_calls=129 distinct_nodes=129 cache_hits=96`, all 7 runs identical) — `total_calls` (now counted only on a cache MISS) dropped from 225 to exactly 129, i.e. `total_calls == distinct_nodes` after the fix, on every run. This is the mechanical proof the redundancy this row targeted is now fully eliminated, not partially: no further duplicate quantize call exists anywhere in the step (staged or unbatched) for this checkpoint's graph shape.

**Correctness, byte-for-byte.** `generated_text="Here is a simple Python function that returns"` on every one of 14 runs (7 with the fix live, 7 with it forced off via a temporary in-place A/B toggle, reverted before landing — see below) — identical across all 14, confirming the cache changes zero floating-point or int8 arithmetic, only which bytes get re-derived vs reused.

**Measured, min-of-7, release profile, `proxima-model-interop --features std,instrument`, harness `runs_a_cached_greedy_decode_loop_and_reports_per_token_wall_clock` (`--ignored --nocapture`), `PROXIMA_MAX_TOKENS=8`, representative step=4 (`cached_len_before=35, new_count=1`) — same protocol as ROW 139's baseline table.** This session's host was NOT quiet: load average climbed from ~10 (session start) to 25-59 (1m) during this row's own measurement window, an order of magnitude noisier than ROW 139's own baseline capture. Per this task's own instruction ("report the noise, do not wait for it"), both sets below are reported in full, including the outliers.

**A/B protocol used to isolate the change from the host-noise drift:** rather than compare this row's post-fix numbers against ROW 139's own baseline table (captured under a materially different, quieter load window — an invalid comparison per `/guiding-principles`' "never compare... your warm cache to their cold one" analogue for load), the fix was temporarily forced off in-place (`None::<&Arc<[u8]>>` substituted for the real cache lookup, a one-line, clearly-marked, git-diffable toggle — never committed) and 7 fresh "before" runs were captured in the SAME few-minute window as the "after" set, immediately following it. The "before" window (load 42.65-59.17) was measurably NOISIER than the "after" window (load 25.62-29.26) — i.e. the comparison is biased AGAINST the fix, not for it, which strengthens rather than weakens any signal that survives it.

| kernel_ms | 38.379 / 43.082 / 328.089, CoV **100.99%** | 39.268 / 44.271 / 58.674, CoV **15.02%** | same host-noise contamination; `kernel_ms` is cohort dot-product time, which this fix does not touch at all — no mechanism predicts a change here, and none is claimed |

**What this measurement DOES and DOES NOT support.** DOES: `residual_ms` — the bucket that contains activation-quantize time, among other things — dropped by a margin larger than its own measurement noise on both sides of the comparison, in the direction this fix's mechanism predicts, under a load comparison biased against it. DOES NOT: a token-level (`evaluate_ms`) or kernel-level claim — the host's own noise this session (CoV > 100% on both) makes that comparison uninformative, not favorable or unfavorable. This is stated as a genuine gap, not softened: **the fix demonstrably does what it claims (96 fewer quantize computations/step, proven by the cache-hit counter) and moves the one clean-signal term in the predicted direction, but does not yet have a clean `evaluate_ms` number behind it.** A rerun on a quieter box is the direct fix for that gap; not attempted further this session per the task's own "do not wait for quiet" instruction.

**Allocation budget, as stated and as measured.** Stated (before implementation): a cache hit should be allocation-**reducing** relative to today's unconditional-fresh-`Vec` baseline (which already allocates once per call regardless, 225 allocations/step) — replacing up to 96 of those 225 allocations with an `Arc` clone (an atomic increment, no allocation) rather than a fresh heap buffer. Not separately re-measured via a tracking allocator this row (the existing `instrument` feature has no allocation-counting facility for this path); the claim rests on the mechanism (`Arc::clone` is documented, standard-library behavior, not a fresh allocation) rather than a counted number, and is flagged as such rather than asserted as measured.

## ROW 141 — mid-flight correction on ROW 140's own cache: `NodeId` is a positional index, not a map key; `BTreeMap` replaced by direct-indexed `Vec` in BOTH the real hot-path cache and the instrument-only diagnostic counter it shares a call site with; re-measured residual_ms shows NO additional signal beyond ROW 140's own already-landed win

Flagged mid-task by the coordinating agent reading ROW 140's own diff: `MatmulStagePlan::activation_q8k`'s cache (`cpu.rs`) and the redundant-quantize-call diagnostic (`instrument.rs`) were both keyed by `NodeId` through a `BTreeMap`, paying an `O(log n)` key-comparison chain per lookup on a path ROW 140 itself measured a `-1.104 ms` residual delta from. Verified before acting, not taken on the message's word alone: `NodeId(pub u32)` is a position in the program's own flat `Vec<Op>` (`op.rs:9-13`'s own doc, `pub struct NodeId(pub u32)` at `op.rs:28`), and `evaluate_quantized_with_scratch` already exploits exactly this fact for `buffers` (`vec![None; program.len()]`, indexed by `node.0 as usize`, `cpu.rs:602`/`614`) — so a `BTreeMap<NodeId, _>` next to that same function was a real, checkable regression against the shape the file already uses, not a stylistic preference.

**Fix 1 (the real hot path, `cohort-staged-graph`-gated, live in every production build with that feature — not `instrument`-gated).** `staged_quantize_cache: BTreeMap<NodeId, Arc<[u8]>>` → `Vec<Option<Arc<[u8]>>>`, sized `vec![None; program.len()]` once per `evaluate_quantized_with_scratch` call (`cpu.rs:727`), threaded as `&mut [Option<Arc<[u8]>>]` through `run_staged_batch`/`build_matmul_stage_plan` (both signatures changed from `&mut BTreeMap<NodeId, Arc<[u8]>>`). Lookup/insert both become direct-indexed (`quantize_cache[activation_node.0 as usize]`), O(1) instead of O(log 129).

**Fix 2 (the instrument-only diagnostic counter, `QUANTIZE_ACTIVATION_CALLS_BY_NODE`, `instrument.rs`).** Confirmed live in the exact measured configuration before touching it: every measurement this row and ROW 139/140 report runs `--features std,instrument`, and `record_quantize_activation_call` (the `Mutex<BTreeMap>` writer) sits *inside* `STAGED_MATMUL_QUANTIZE_TICKS`'s own timed span (`cpu.rs:3233` reads ticks before the call at `3239`, `3242-3245` reads elapsed after `quantize_row_q8k_dispatch` returns) — so its own cost (mutex lock + BTreeMap insert) was folded into `residual_ms` on every one of ROW 140's 129 post-fix miss calls/step, not free background bookkeeping. `Mutex<BTreeMap<NodeId, u64>>` → `Mutex<Vec<u64>>`, grown once (`resize(index + 1, 0)`) to cover the largest node id seen, zeroed (not reallocated) on `reset_step`. The `Mutex` itself stays — both call sites (`build_matmul_stage_plan`, `run_reduce_quantized`) run on the leader thread only, serially, strictly before any cohort round opens, so there is never real contention to eliminate, only the O(log n) traversal — replacing it with an `UnsafeCell` single-writer invariant would trade a proven-uncontended lock for an unsafe invariant this diagnostic has no reason to take on.

## ROW 146 — rung 1/2 NOT landed: the mechanism is a stride gate tripped by conv's own shape-inference marker tensor, not a missing GEMM detector

**What was expected going in (task brief):** "cpu.rs's generic index-map interpreter walks it scalar — no GEMM routing" implying no fast-path routing exists at all for matmul-shaped folds. **Partially refuted by reading the code, not inferred:** a fast-path router for matmul-shaped `Keep::Reduce` folds already exists and is already unconditionally engaged for EVERY `Keep::Reduce` node in `run_reduce` (`cpu.rs:4126` doc: "The dense f32 GEMM interpreter: NEON dot/width tiles then a generic fallback") — plain (non-conv) matmuls already route through `neon_tile_plan`/`gemm_tile_neon` (a ported ggml-tinyBLAS 6x4 NEON microkernel) when their shape qualifies. mnist's own linear layers were not separately measured this session (mnist's forward is dominated by its 2 conv layers, see below), so whether they individually reach the tile is not directly confirmed here, but the routing infrastructure itself is real and present, not absent.

**What actually gates conv's own materialized-window `Reduce` out of every fast path, traced to the exact function and line, not asserted:**

1. `proxima-onnx/src/lower.rs:2234` (`window_axis`) builds each windowed spatial dim as a **2-term** `AxisIndex` (`AxisTerm::scaled(out_axis, stride)` + `AxisTerm::scaled(kernel_axis, dilation)`) — this is genuinely still affine (each individual logical axis contributes a constant physical stride; `View::stride(dim)` is well-defined per axis even here), confirmed by reading `bind.rs:790` (`IndexMap::Affine(pattern) => (node, layout_of(pattern, ...), None)` — the windowed image operand resolves with `gather: None`, i.e. it is NOT classified as a gather at all, contrary to what "the window is basically a gather" would predict).
2. The actual trip wire is `lower.rs:2318`'s own **stamp** tensor — `window_materialize`'s all-ones `Op::Constant` of shape `[out_h, out_w, kh, kw]`, present purely so `shape::infer`'s `unify_iteration_space` (which only resolves an axis's extent from a *pure single-term* projection) can resolve `oh/ow/kh/kw`'s extents at all (that function's own doc says so explicitly: "the stamp is not decoration"). This stamp is read via a **pure single-term projection** (`projection(6, &[2,3,4,5])`), so per-dimension it passes `operand_is_affine` (`cpu.rs:4884`) cleanly — but its physical stride along the iteration space's LAST (innermost) output axis is the stamp tensor's OWN row-major stride for that axis, which for a `[out_h,out_w,kh,kw]`-shaped constant is `kh*kw` (25 for mnist's first conv's 5x5 kernel) — far greater than the `<= 1` `operand_is_unit_or_broadcast` (`cpu.rs:4901-4903`) requires.
3. `body_shape_is_affine_fast_path` (`cpu.rs:4914`) requires EVERY operand of a `Binary` body to pass `operand_is_unit_or_broadcast` — the stamp's own stride (25, not <=1) fails this regardless of whether the actual IMAGE operand's own window-axis stride would have qualified on its own. **One operand — a marker tensor whose entire numeric contribution is multiplying by 1.0 — sinks the whole fold's fast-path eligibility.**
4. Downstream, both `fast_path` and `reduction_fast_path` (`cpu.rs:4198-4200`) are `false` for every one of these nodes, so `neon_tile_plan` (the actual NEON 6x4 tile) is never even attempted (`cpu.rs:4281`, gated `if reduction_fast_path`) and `try_run_width_tile` never fires either — both silently fall through to `Path::Generic`, the fully scalar per-element interpreter with a `gather_cursors` `Option` check on every read.

**Measured consequence:** `evaluate_quantized`'s own per-node-kind diagnostic (`cpu.rs`'s `DIAG evaluate_quantized node_kind=` line, read via the `mnist-diag` companion) shows `reduce_f32_dense` (mnist's 7 matmul/conv folds combined) at **85.7-94.2% of total forward wall time** across repeated runs this session, at 5.27-8.76 ns/element in quieter moments (up to 73 ns/element under host load spikes) for what should be a single FMA. `neon_dot_tile: gate_passes≈1/image, invocations=0/image` (the gate structurally admits the shape as a *candidate* via a separate, coarser check, then the tile's own leading-row/width-column thresholds reject it before a single real tile call fires) confirms zero SIMD engagement anywhere in this model's forward pass.

**Why this was NOT fixed this session (bounded-fix test, per AGENTS.md):** the smallest safe fix identified — teach `operand_is_unit_or_broadcast` (or a sibling check reachable from `body_shape_is_affine_fast_path`) to recognize "this operand is a `Constant` with a uniform value the multiply body would leave unchanged (1.0 for `Multiply`)" and exclude it from the stride gate entirely — requires plumbing operand-VALUE information into a function that today only inspects `strides`/`gather` shape metadata, a genuine (not cosmetic) change to one of this crate's most heavily-tested, correctness-critical hot-path gates, shared by every `Keep::Reduce`/`Keep::Scan` fold in the whole crate (LLM decode/prefill included, per `docs/discipline.md`'s own preceding 144 rows). It is not expressible as a bounded, obviously-safe <50-line patch inside the remaining session budget with the validation depth (442+ `proxima-tensor` tests, workspace clippy, the full gate script) this repo requires before landing a hot-path change — it is exactly the "large, contested" category `AGENTS.md` reserves for a scoped follow-up rather than a same-turn patch. **NOT ROLLED BACK (nothing was landed to roll back) — flagged with the precise fix location, not silently punted.**

**What a correct fix would need to prove, named for the next session:** (a) that skipping a genuine `Constant(1.0)` operand from `operand_is_unit_or_broadcast`'s stride check cannot change results for ANY other `Keep::Reduce`/`Keep::Scan` site in the crate that happens to multiply by a literal-1.0 constant for unrelated reasons (a full-crate semantic audit, not just this call site); (b) that once the stamp stops sinking the gate, the IMAGE operand's OWN window-axis stride (mnist's own conv strides, most likely stride=1 first layer) actually qualifies `operand_is_unit_or_broadcast` on its own merits — this session did not measure that stride directly and it is stated as a plausible-but-unverified next check, not a fact; (c) a full re-bench against this row's own sealed baseline (ROW 145) to confirm the scalar-fast-path win before ever touching the NEON tile layer.

**Phase-2 charter (owner-requested framing, evidence FOR/AGAINST, not a plan committed to):**
- **(a) Shape-specialized FSM loop nests over generic library-call mimicry:** evidence FOR — this session's own mechanism finding (above) shows the blocker is a SHAPE-INFERENCE ARTIFACT (the stamp), not an inherent shape mismatch with the existing tile machinery; a shape-specialized unrolled FMA loop for the *known-small*, *bind-time-static* conv kernel extents (5x5=25, 3x3=9) sidesteps the stamp/stride-gate question entirely by never routing through the generic multi-operand interpreter for this node shape at all — plausible, unmeasured. Evidence AGAINST/open: no code was written to test this, so "would beat the existing tile machinery" is asserted nowhere, only that it is architecturally a smaller, more surgical, higher-confidence target than repairing the general-purpose stride gate.
- **(b) Cross-op tile streaming (conv/matmul -> relu without materializing the intermediate):** NOT probed this session (owner's own instruction scoped this to "if budget remains after rung 3" — rung 3 was never reached). `bind.rs`'s existing Reduce-absorbs-Elementwise fusion (the `element_body`/`ComposedBody` mechanism already visible throughout this file, e.g. `build_reduce_op`'s `element_body` parameter) is real, existing precedent that such fusion is architecturally native to this crate's `BoundOp` design, but whether extending it across the conv-then-activation boundary is a small or large change was not investigated.

**Not landed. No rollback (nothing shipped). No source diff to this row beyond the sealed bench (ROW 145) and its companion diagnostic.**

- `sed -n '4884,4923p' proxima-tensor/src/cpu.rs` — `operand_is_affine`/`operand_is_unit_or_broadcast`/`body_shape_is_affine_fast_path`
- `sed -n '782,810p' proxima-tensor/src/bind.rs` — `build_operand`, confirming the windowed operand resolves `gather: None`
- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<scratch> cargo run --release -p proxima-onnx --example mnist_diag --features mnist-diag` and grep `"DIAG evaluate_quantized node_kind="` / `"neon_dot_tile"` — reproduces the 85.7-94.2% `reduce_f32_dense` share and the zero-tile-invocation finding

## ROW 147 — identity-multiply elimination lands (class fix, both fusion entry points); the stamp stops sinking the gate, but a SEPARATE, pre-existing mechanism (`quarantine_broadcast_operands`) still sinks conv's dominant reduce cost — named, not papered over

Repo: `/Users/brianbruggeman/repos/slot-0/proxima-wt-perf`, branch `perf/conv-stamp-fastpath`, off `6e273771806451a6ecde4c1288012ad21799c6d7` (ROW 145/146's own sealed HEAD). `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` pinned to a scratchpad dir for every command. Host: Apple M1 Max, macOS, arm64. Build profile: `dev` for tests/clippy, `release`/`bench` for the sealed bench and `mnist_diag` — never mixed with the correctness runs. Debug build for bind.rs's own unit tests (relevant to ROW 147's own bug-catch below: the empty-`ComposedBody` panic only reproduced in a debug build's `usize` underflow check).

**Chosen fix: (A) identity-multiply elimination at bind time**, `proxima-tensor/src/bind.rs`. Options B and C were evaluated first, by reading the code, and rejected with evidence — not assumed:

- **(B) teach `operand_is_unit_or_broadcast` to accept a Constant-source operand regardless of stride — REJECTED, refuted by reading `BoundOpKind::Constant`'s own executor.** `cpu.rs:2121` (`run_constant`) and `cpu.rs:11274`/`11525` (`run_constant_typed`) confirm a bound `Constant` is materialized as a REAL, densely-written buffer ("an executor writes `value` to every element of `BoundOp::extents`") — not a lazily-broadcast scalar. So B's own premise ("constant memory has no locality cost") is false as stated: accepting the stride at the gate would still pay a real strided read every element. Worse, for `Conv` specifically B does not even reach the stride check: the fused body for `product = windowed * weight` where `windowed = image * stamp` is a genuine 2-step chain (`Multiply(Multiply(image,stamp),weight)`), and `body_shape()` (`cpu.rs:4850`) classifies ANY body with more than 1 step as `BodyShape::Generic` — `body_shape_is_affine_fast_path`'s `Generic => false` arm (`cpu.rs:4922`) rejects it before any operand's stride is ever inspected. B cannot fix a defect it never reaches.
- **(C) lower-side: give the stamp broadcast-shaped strides — REJECTED, narrower AND does not fix the dominant cost either.** Even a perfectly-strided stamp leaves the SAME 2-step fused chain (`windowed` is still a distinct `Multiply` step nested inside `product`'s own `Multiply`), so `body_shape()` still classifies it `Generic` regardless of any operand's stride — C does not collapse the chain depth, which turned out (see the negative finding below) to not even be the dominant defect once traced further. C also only touches `window_materialize`'s one call site; `window_materialize1d`, `window_materialize3d`, and `valid_window_count` (`proxima-onnx/src/lower.rs:2368,2416,3239,3378,3586`) mint the identical all-ones stamp independently and would each need their own repair — the class-fix framing (any future ×1 marker gets the same treatment) is unavailable to C by construction.

**Implementation.** `proxima-tensor/src/bind.rs`: a new `eliminate_identity_multiply(body, operands, ones) -> Option<(NodeId, &IndexMap)>` helper returns the surviving operand when `body == ScalarOp::Multiply` and exactly one of the two operands is a node the builder recorded as `Op::Constant{value: 1.0}` (`ones: RefCell<Vec<bool>>`, grown one entry per `BoundOpBuilder::push` call — an incremental, sans-IO-honoring per-node flag, not a `&[Op]` slice threaded through the fusion recursion, since this module's own doc states the builder must not require the whole program in hand). The check is applied at **both** fusion entry points that can encounter a held `Multiply` body — `compose_operand` (the nested-fusion-recursion path) and `compose` (the standalone-materialization path `materialize_if_held`/`quarantine_broadcast_operands` reach). Landing only in `compose_operand` (the first attempt) measured zero improvement on the dominant cost; see the mechanism finding below for why the second site was necessary. `compose_fused_operands` and `compose` both guarantee the returned `ComposedBody` has at least one step even when elimination empties it (wrapping the survivor in a trailing `Identity` step) — see the correctness-audit bug-catch below.

**Correctness audit (full, before landing — the reason the prior session declined to patch the gate directly).**

1. **Enumerated every `Op::Constant` construction site** in `proxima-onnx/src/lower.rs` (`grep -n "Op::Constant"`, 19 sites). Every `value: 1.0` site (`window_materialize` 2332, `window_materialize1d` 2368, `window_materialize3d` 2416, `valid_window_count`'s two `ones` tensors 3239/3378, and 3586) exists for the identical shape-inference-stamp purpose `window_materialize`'s own doc names, all feeding a `ScalarOp::Multiply` — none is a scale factor or any other numerically load-bearing constant. The elimination is gated strictly to `body == ScalarOp::Multiply`; a `Constant{value: 1.0}` used as an `Add`/`Subtract`/`Divide` operand elsewhere in the crate is untouched (`1.0` is not the identity for those ops).
2. **Position-invariance is the soundness argument, not the specific stamp shape.** `BoundOpKind::Constant`'s own executor (`run_constant`/`run_constant_typed`) writes `value` to every element regardless of position — so dropping a `Constant(1.0)` `Multiply` operand is sound for ANY `IndexMap` it carries (broadcast, projection, or the window-axis pattern this stamp uses), not merely the one pattern this session traced. This is the class-fix property: any future `×1.0` marker constant, from any lowering, gets the identical treatment automatically.
3. **The iteration space cannot be affected.** `build_reduce_op`/`build_elementwise_op` compute `extents = shapes.of(node).to_vec()` from the NODE's own already-resolved shape (from `shape::infer`, which runs strictly before `bind::bind`) — independent of what `compose`/`compose_operand` do to the body. Confirmed by reading both call sites: `extents` is computed BEFORE `compose(...)`/`compose_fused_operands(...)` ever runs, from a wholly separate data source. Eliminating a body operand cannot change a node's output shape.
4. **Numerical exactness.** `x * 1.0 == x` bit-for-bit for every finite, `+-inf` (the `ReduceInit::NegativeInfinity` `MaxPool` padding case specifically named in `lower.rs`'s own doc as relying on this), and quiet-NaN `f32` value under IEEE 754 — the one stated caveat is signaling-NaN quieting on multiply, irrelevant to any real image/weight/activation this crate ever binds (MEASURED as a non-issue: no test corpus or the sealed bench's real MNIST bytes carry an sNaN).
5. **A real bug the audit caught before landing, not after:** the first implementation (elimination only in `compose_operand`) fully eliminates `MaxPool`/`AveragePool`'s `windowed` node when it is `reduce.operand` DIRECTLY (no further `Multiply` wraps it, unlike `Conv`'s `product`), leaving `ComposedBody.steps` EMPTY. `apply_body`'s `step_values[body.steps.len() - 1]` (`cpu.rs:10367`) then underflows in a debug build ("attempt to subtract with overflow"), caught immediately by `proxima-onnx`'s own `lower::tests::averagepool_padded_count_include_pad_zero_excludes_padding_from_the_divisor` (and 4 sibling AveragePool/MaxPool tests) going red on the first `cargo nextest run -p proxima-onnx --all-features` after the change — not discovered later, not shipped and rolled back. Fixed by having `compose_fused_operands` (and, after the second fix below, `compose`) guarantee at least one step, matching the existing `ComposedBody::leaf(ScalarOp::Identity)` convention the no-fusion branch already uses.
6. **omega's parity suite is part of the oracle set** (per task) since omega executes the same `BoundOp`s: `cargo nextest run -p omega --all-features --no-fail-fast` — 138 run, 135 passed, 3 failed. **All 3 failures reproduced BIT-IDENTICAL on the unmodified baseline** via `git stash`/`git stash pop` A-B (same `max_relative_diff=0.07260467` for the wgpu f16 test, same `cpu=0.16142446` vs `reference=0.1850988` for the Metal tiled-gemm test) — pre-existing Metal/wgpu f16-precision parity gaps, unrelated to this bind-time change, not newly introduced. Reported, not buried.

**Mechanism finding (the negative/mixed result — the number did NOT move commensurately, profiled per the task's own instruction, not hand-waved).** A temporary, since-removed `eprintln!` instrument (verified removed via `git diff` before commit) traced the actual composed body for mnist's 4 conv/pool-shaped reduce folds (`node_kind=reduce_f32_dense`, 3-dim reduction over `ci×kh×kw`):

- **The step-chain collapse the fix targets DID work**: all 4 nodes now show `steps=1, shape=Binary` (was implicitly a 2-step `Generic` body before, per ROW 146's own `body_shape()` reasoning re-derived this session) — the class fix genuinely fires and genuinely removes the stamp from the fused body.
- **But `fast_path` is STILL `false` for all 4**, for a mechanism ROW 146 did not reach: `quarantine_broadcast_operands` (`bind.rs`, pre-existing, unrelated to the stamp) force-materializes `windowed` as its OWN standalone buffer whenever its extent (`[n,c,oh,ow,kh,kw]`, EXCLUDING the output-channel broadcast axis `co`) is smaller than the consuming reduce's full iteration extent (`[n,co,oh,ow,ci,kh,kw]`, ×8 output channels for mnist's first conv) — a legitimate existing cost guard (recomputing `windowed`'s body once per `co` repetition would be strictly worse). Once `windowed` materializes standalone, its buffer has INTRINSIC row-major im2col strides (measured: ox-stride=9=`kh×kw`, kh-stride=3=`kw`, matching a fresh `[n,c,26,26,3,3]` buffer's own row-major layout for mnist's first 3×3 conv) that fail `operand_is_unit_or_broadcast`'s `stride <= 1` requirement — REGARDLESS of whether the buffer's values were produced by a `Multiply`-by-stamp (before this fix) or a plain `Identity` copy (after this fix). The elimination makes `windowed`'s OWN materialization cheaper (one copy instead of one multiply-against-a-freshly-read-stamp-buffer) but cannot change the fact that a MATERIALIZED windowed buffer's physical layout is never width-stride-1 for the reduce that consumes it. This is a genuinely NEW, deeper finding than ROW 146's: the stamp and the quarantine-forced materialization are two INDEPENDENT causes stacked on the same node, and only the first is fixed here.
- Confirmed the first implementation attempt (elimination in `compose_operand` only) measured **zero** change to `reduce_f32_dense`'s ns/element, because `quarantine_broadcast_operands` removes `windowed` from `held` before the reduce's own fusion ever recurses into it — `compose_operand`'s elimination never got a chance to run. Extending the identical check to `compose`'s own top-level entry (where `quarantine_broadcast_operands`'s forced materialization actually lands) was required to get ANY measurable effect at all.

## ROW 148 — a genuinely NEW, deeper blocker found for `Conv` (the tile's own single-shared-leading-axis assumption, not just the stride gate ROW 147 named); the narrower, provably-safe multi-dim-reduction case that DOES qualify lands and moves `reduce_f32_dense` measurably, but total ms/image barely moves because `Conv` — 3 of the 4 still-`Generic` folds — stays out of scope for BOTH existing NEON tiles regardless of the reduction-stride fix

Repo: `/Users/brianbruggeman/repos/slot-0/proxima-wt-neon`, branch `perf/conv-neon-route`, off `6fa7fc39008ab5741c700428b34182575a811b2b` (ROW 147's own sealed HEAD). `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` pinned to a scratchpad dir for every command below. Host: Apple M1 Max, macOS, arm64. Build profile: `dev` for tests/clippy, `release`/`bench` for the sealed bench and `mnist_diag` — never mixed with the correctness runs.

**Mechanism, traced by adding a temporary, since-removed `eprintln!` in `run_reduce` and running `mnist_diag` against the real model (git-diff-verified removed before this row's commit, same discipline ROW 147 used) — not inferred from reading alone.** All 4 of the still-`Generic` `Keep::Reduce` folds this initiative targets were dumped with their `leading_output_axes`, `reduction_dims`, `extents`, and every operand's per-dimension stride:

```
leading_output_axes=[0,1,2] last_output_dim=Some(3) reduction_dims=[4,5,6] extents=[1,8,26,26,1,3,3]   operand_strides=[[6084,0,234,9,6084,3,1],[0,9,0,0,9,3,1]]   (Conv layer 1, ci=1)
leading_output_axes=[0,1,2] last_output_dim=Some(3) reduction_dims=[4,5,6] extents=[1,16,24,24,8,3,3]  operand_strides=[[41472,0,216,9,5184,3,1],[0,72,0,0,9,3,1]]  (Conv layer 2, ci=8)
leading_output_axes=[0,1,2] last_output_dim=Some(3) reduction_dims=[4,5,6] extents=[1,24,22,22,16,3,3] operand_strides=[[69696,0,198,9,4356,3,1],[0,144,0,0,9,3,1]] (Conv layer 3, ci=16)
leading_output_axes=[0]     last_output_dim=Some(1) reduction_dims=[2,3,4] extents=[1,32,24,22,22]     operand_strides=[[11616,0,484,22,1],[0,11616,484,22,1]]     (FC layer 1, no explicit flatten)
```

Axis order for the 3 `Conv` rows is `(n,co,oy,ox,ci,ky,kx)`; for the FC row, `(n,out_features,c,h,w)`.

1. **`Conv`'s reduction (`ci,ky,kx`) is genuinely blocked, not merely stride-gated — confirms and sharpens ROW 147's own finding.** For every `Conv` row, the windowed operand's trailing two reduction dims (`ky,kx`) compose contiguously with each other (`ky`-stride == `kx`-extent × `kx`-stride, e.g. layer 1: `3 == 3×1`), but the outermost reduction dim (`ci`) does not extend that chain — its stride (`6084`/`5184`/`4356`) is nowhere near `ky`-extent × `ky`-stride (`9` in every row), because `windowed`'s own materialized layout is `[n,c,oh,ow,kh,kw]` — `c` sits OUTSIDE `oh,ow` in memory (ROW 147's own finding), so incrementing `ci` jumps a whole `oh*ow*kh*kw`-sized block, not the adjacent `kh*kw` one a flat walk would need. The weight operand's own reduction (`ci,ky,kx`) strides are `9,3,1` in every one of the 3 layers (all three use a 3x3 kernel) — `stride(ci) == kh*kw` exactly, matching the extent product a flat walk needs — so weight IS fully contiguous — weight's `[co,ci,kh,kw]` storage genuinely IS row-major over exactly `(ci,ky,kx)` — but a fast-path gate here requires BOTH body operands to qualify, and windowed never does. **This was already ROW 147's conclusion; this row's contribution is confirming it with real measured strides instead of the prior row's derivation, and finding it is not the ONLY blocker (next point).**
2. **A second, independent, and NEWLY-found blocker: `neon_tile_plan` (the dot tile) and `width_tile_plan` (the width tile) BOTH additionally require `leading_output_axes.len() == 1`** (`cpu.rs:5978`, `cpu.rs:5469`) — a precondition ROW 146/147 never reached because the stride gate already failed first. `Conv`'s own `output_axes` is rank-4 `(n,co,oy,ox)`; `output_axes_split` (`cpu.rs:2260`) puts everything but the last axis into `leading_output_axes`, so `Conv`'s leading is `(n,co,oy)` — **3 axes, structurally, regardless of any stride fix.** Worse than a simple arity mismatch: the measured strides show `windowed` and `weight` depend on *disjoint* subsets of those 3 axes — `weight`'s only non-zero leading-axis stride is on `co` (`windowed`'s own `co`-stride is `0`, a pure broadcast), while `windowed`'s non-zero leading-axis strides are on `n`/`oy` (`weight`'s own `n`- and `oy`-strides are `0`). Both tile kernels compute a *single* `row_stride`/`col_stride` per operand from `leading_output_axes[0]` alone (`cpu.rs:5496`, `cpu.rs:6003`) — a design that assumes one shared "row" axis both operands walk together, exactly the GEMM shape a plain matmul has and `Conv` genuinely does not: `Conv`'s "row" concept splits across two operands with non-overlapping ownership of the leading axes. This is not a stride-pattern relaxation away from being fixed — it requires the tile kernel itself to understand a per-operand-owned multi-axis leading structure, a change to the register-tiled loop nest (panel/row-remainder logic included), not to a gate. **Named here as the actual remaining blocker, more precise than either ROW 146's or ROW 147's own framing, and out of this session's bounded-fix budget for the same reason ROW 146 declined its own smaller gate change: AGENTS.md's bar for a hot-path change shared by every `Keep::Reduce` fold in the crate.**
3. **The FC-without-flatten row (`reduction_dims=[2,3,4]`, 3 dims) is a DIFFERENT, provably-safe case that DOES qualify**, once its `leading_output_axes.len() == 1` is already true (`[0]`, satisfied) and its reduction dims compose fully flat for BOTH operands: `2,3,4` (`c,h,w`) strides `484,22,1` on the activation and `484,22,1` on the weight — identical, and the outer dim's stride (`484`) equals the inner block's own product (`22×22`), i.e. the WHOLE reduction is one contiguous `24×22×22 = 11616`-element flat span for both operands, not merely its trailing two dims. This is the shape the fix below targets.

**Chosen fix: generalize the reduce executor's OWN contraction-dim fast-path gate (`reduction_strides`/`reduction_fast_path` in `run_reduce`, `cpu.rs`) from "exactly one reduction dim, stride 1" to "the WHOLE `reduction_dims` range composes as one contiguous stride-1 span, for this operand" — executor-internal, no new `Op`/`ScalarOp`/`IndexMap`, and it reuses `neon_tile_plan`/`gemm_tile_neon` and `reduce_dot_fast` 100% unchanged** (their own inputs — `reduction_strides[operand] == 1` and `reduction_total` — already generalize correctly; only the value that FEEDS them needed to widen). Rejected alternatives, evaluated first:

- **Blocked (2-level: outer × contiguous-inner) reduction generalization of `gemm_tile_neon`/`neon_tile_plan`, to also unlock `Conv` — NOT attempted this session, named as the real next step.** Mechanically sound (`gemm_tile_neon`'s own doc already states a caller may re-invoke it into the same `out` buffer to accumulate a running total, which is exactly what a per-`ci`-block outer loop would need — zero kernel-body changes), but blocked on finding #2 above: `neon_tile_plan`'s `leading_output_axes.len() == 1` / single-shared-row-axis assumption fails FIRST, independent of the reduction shape, so generalizing the reduction alone would not be sufficient to unlock `Conv` — the leading-axis assumption would ALSO need generalizing (a genuinely different, larger piece of surgery: the row-tiled loop nest itself, not a stride gate), and combining both in one session, on the crate's most heavily-shared hot-path interpreter, exceeds this session's bounded-fix budget for the same reason ROW 146 declined a smaller version of this same call.
- **Loosening `quarantine_broadcast_operands` (bind.rs) for this shape — REJECTED, doesn't reach the real blocker.** `quarantine_broadcast_operands` exists (its own doc, `bind.rs:707-718`) to stop a `Keep::Reduce` fold from re-running a held operand's own fusion body once per broadcast repetition it would otherwise be forced to replay (`co` times for `Conv`'s `windowed`) — a real, load-bearing correctness-adjacent COST guard, not a correctness bug: skipping it would make `windowed`'s multiply-by-stamp-turned-identity body re-evaluate `co`× more elementwise work than materializing once. Loosening it would only change WHERE `windowed`'s bytes come from (inline-recomputed vs. standalone-materialized) — its PHYSICAL LAYOUT once bound is unaffected either way (`bind_operand`'s output layout is a function of the node's own resolved shape, not of whether it fused), so this would not change the `ci`-axis stride-gate failure #1 measured above at all. Confirms ROW 147's own prior rejection of a closely related idea (option C) on the same grounds, now with real strides instead of a derivation.

**Implementation.** `proxima-tensor/src/cpu.rs`, `run_reduce`. New helper `reduction_is_fully_flat(resolved, reduction_dims, operand_index) -> bool`: walks `reduction_dims` innermost-to-outermost, checking `stride(dim) == expected` where `expected` accumulates the row-major product of every extent nested inside it (`reduction_dims.len() == 1` degenerates to exactly today's original `stride(dims[0]) == 1` check, unchanged). `reduction_strides` (previously `Vec::new()` whenever `reduction_dims.len() != 1`) is now built for every operand via this helper, `1` when it qualifies, `i64::MAX` otherwise — a value `operand_is_affine`/`operand_is_unit_or_broadcast`'s own `>= 0` / `<= 1` checks reject unconditionally, so a non-flat operand fails exactly as before, just via a real sentinel instead of an empty table. `reduction_fast_path`'s own gate changed from `reduction_dims.len() == 1` to `!reduction_dims.is_empty()` — the ONLY other line touched. `neon_tile_plan`, `gemm_tile_neon`, `reduce_dot_fast`, and `width_tile_plan` are byte-for-byte unchanged; `reduction_total` (already computed as the full product over `reduction_extents`, never just `reduction_dims[0]`'s own extent) already fed them the right value.

**Correctness reasoning.** `reduction_is_fully_flat` is a pure stride-pattern predicate over already-resolved `View`/`extents` data — it cannot itself produce a wrong VALUE, only a wrong ELIGIBILITY decision, and a false-positive there would only be caught by a genuinely different physical layout satisfying the row-major chain by coincidence while not actually being one contiguous span, which is impossible by construction (the chain check IS the definition of row-major contiguity — `expected` is recomputed from the SAME `resolved.extents` the `View`'s own strides were built against, not a separate source that could drift). Every downstream consumer (`neon_tile_plan`'s own `reduction_strides[index] != 1` check, `reduce_dot_fast`'s `OperandSpan{stride: reduction_strides[index] as usize}`) already existed and is unmodified; they were built for a `stride == 1` flat span, and `reduction_is_fully_flat`'s only job is to correctly widen WHICH shapes get to claim `1`. No change to `Op`/`ScalarOp`/`IndexMap`, no change to `bind.rs`/`lower.rs` — the fix is confined to `run_reduce`'s own local gate.

**Charter correction, stated up front because the pre-registered design was wrong and the diagnostic is what showed it.** The task's own framing ("the materialized windowed buffer as the im2col matrix") assumes `windowed`'s standalone layout is a valid flat `[N, K]` matrix once `(n,oy,ox)` is treated as rows. **It is not** — `window_materialize` (`proxima-onnx/src/lower.rs:2320`) declares `windowed`'s own shape `[n,c,oh,ow,kh,kw]`, so `c` sits OUTSIDE `oh,ow` in memory (ROW 147/148's own finding, re-confirmed this session — see the diagnostic below). Treating `(n,oy,ox)` as GEMM rows over the WHOLE `K=ci*ky*kx` range would read across a `ci`-sized memory gap mid-row. The buffer genuinely IS a valid GEMM operand, just not as one flat `[N,K]` span: for a FIXED `ci`, the block `windowed[n,ci,:,:,:,:]` — `(oy,ox,ky,kx)` nested row-major with no other axis between — reshapes losslessly to a contiguous `[N=oy·ox, K'=ky·kw]` matrix, and `weight[:,ci,:,:]` reshapes the same way to `[M=co, K'=9]`. The correct design is `sum over ci of (weight[:,ci,:,:] @ windowed[n,ci,:,:,:,:]^T)` — the "blocked (2-level: outer x contiguous-inner)" shape ROW 148 itself named as the real next step and explicitly left unattempted pending a second, independent blocker (below). This row implements exactly that, not the single-im2col-matrix framing the charter opened with.

**The verified `windowed`-buffer layout, from a real diagnostic this session (temporary `eprintln!` in the new `conv_gemm_tile_plan` call site, git-diff-verified removed before this row's commit — `git diff proxima-tensor/src/cpu.rs | grep DIAG` returns nothing on the committed tree, same discipline ROW 147/148 used), not assumed:**

```
DIAG conv_gemm_tile_plan m_total=8  n_total=676 outer_extent=1  inner_span=9 row_stride_m=9   col_stride_n=9 outer_stride_m=9 outer_stride_n=6084 out_row_stride=676  (Conv layer 1)
DIAG conv_gemm_tile_plan m_total=16 n_total=576 outer_extent=8  inner_span=9 row_stride_m=72  col_stride_n=9 outer_stride_m=9 outer_stride_n=5184 out_row_stride=576  (Conv layer 2)
DIAG conv_gemm_tile_plan m_total=24 n_total=484 outer_extent=16 inner_span=9 row_stride_m=144 col_stride_n=9 outer_stride_m=9 outer_stride_n=4356 out_row_stride=484  (Conv layer 3)
```

Every field matches ROW 148's own raw `operand_strides` dump bit-for-bit once translated: `outer_stride_n` (windowed's own `ci`-stride) equals ROW 148's cited `6084`/`5184`/`4356` exactly; `row_stride_m` (weight's `co`-stride) equals ROW 148's cited `9`/`72`/`144`; `col_stride_n`/`outer_stride_m` (both `9` = `kh·kw`) match the inner-block size both rows independently derived. This is the SAME buffer ROW 147/148 measured, cross-checked from a second, independently-written diagnostic — not re-assumed.

**Mechanism: two independent gaps closed, both named precisely by ROW 148 and neither touched by it.**

1. **The reduction-contiguity gap (ROW 147/148's own finding, re-derived here as a count, not just a bool).** `max_flat_reduction_suffix_len` (renamed/generalized from ROW 148's `reduction_is_fully_flat`, which now degenerates to `== reduction_dims.len()`) walks `reduction_dims` innermost-first and returns how many TRAILING dims compose as one contiguous stride-1 span, instead of only a whole-range bool. For `Conv`: `weight`'s suffix length is 3 (fully flat — `ci`'s stride `9` = `ky_extent·kx_extent`, matching ROW 148's own "weight IS fully contiguous" finding), `windowed`'s is 2 (`ky,kx` only — `ci`'s stride breaks the chain exactly where ROW 148 found it breaks). `inner_len = min(3,2) = 2`; the outer prefix (`reduction_dims[..1] = [ci]`) is the one axis neither operand can flatten away.
2. **The disjoint-leading-axis gap (ROW 148's OWN "genuinely NEW, deeper blocker": `neon_tile_plan`/`width_tile_plan` both require `leading_output_axes.len() == 1`).** `Conv`'s leading axes are `(n,co,oy)` — 3 axes, and the two reduce-body operands own DISJOINT subsets: `weight` varies only with `co` (zero stride on `n,oy,ox`), `windowed` varies only with `n,oy` plus the width axis `ox` (zero stride on `co`). `conv_gemm_tile_plan` (new, `cpu.rs`) finds the single axis (`m_axis`) one operand alone owns, requires the OTHER operand's stride there to be exactly zero, and — the piece that makes the multi-axis case tractable without a second odometer loop — verifies the REMAINING leading axes plus the width axis compose as one contiguous flat `N`-address chain in BOTH the `N`-operand and the reduce's own `out_layout` (`axes_flat_chain`, unit-aware: axes of extent `<= 1`, e.g. `Conv`'s own always-`1` batch axis, are skipped rather than checked, since a never-varying coordinate's stride can never affect an address — this is what stops `n`'s own out-of-chain-order stride in `out_layout`, real but multiplied by an always-zero coordinate, from spuriously failing the gate). When both checks hold, the whole `(n,oy,ox)` space collapses to one flat `N` index with a SINGLE stride (`col_stride_n = inner_span`, exactly `windowed`'s per-position stride ROW 148 already measured), letting `Conv`'s 3-axis leading shape reuse `neon_tile_plan`'s existing 2D row/column tile loop nest UNCHANGED in spirit — only the base-offset formula (now `M`-row × `N`-flat × `outer_extent`-block, not `M`-row × `N`-flat alone) is new.

**Reused, not reinvented: `gemm_tile_neon` itself is 100% byte-for-byte unchanged.** `run_conv_gemm_tile`/`conv_gemm_row_block` (new, `cpu.rs`) call the SAME `unsafe fn gemm_tile_neon<const ROWS: usize>` `neon_tile_plan`'s own dot tile uses, once per `(M tile, N tile, outer ci step)`, into the SAME `tile_out` register array across all `outer_extent` steps — `gemm_tile_neon`'s own doc already states a caller may re-invoke it into the same `out` to accumulate a running total (it reads `*out_value` and ADDS to it), which is exactly the accumulation an outer `ci` loop needs. This is the "blocked (2-level)" rejected alternative ROW 148 named as "mechanically sound... blocked on [the leading-axis gap]" — unblocked here, not redesigned. Row/column remainder tiles reuse the same const-generic monomorphization pattern (`1..=5` leftover rows) the existing dot tile already established; a scalar remainder loop (new, small) covers any leftover `N` columns past the last full `TILE_COLS` block — never exercised by any of `Conv`'s 3 real mnist folds (`n_total` is `676/576/484`, all exact multiples of 4) but not assumed away.

**Detection tried only when both existing gates already declined** (`if !fast_path && !reduction_fast_path`), positioned after the width-tile's own early return and before the existing dot-tile's `tile_plan` computation — by construction (`leading_output_axes.len() < 2` rejects immediately) `conv_gemm_tile_plan` can never steal a node either existing tile already claims, and `neon_tile_plan`/`width_tile_plan`/`gemm_tile_neon`/`reduce_dot_fast`/`width_tile_plan` are all byte-for-byte unchanged outside the one renamed-and-generalized `max_flat_reduction_suffix_len` helper (§ below).

**Correctness reasoning.** `axes_flat_chain` is a pure stride-pattern predicate over already-resolved `View`/`extents` data (same category as ROW 148's own `reduction_is_fully_flat` argument): it cannot produce a wrong VALUE, only a wrong ELIGIBILITY decision, and a false positive would require a physical layout that satisfies the row-major chain by coincidence while not actually being one contiguous span — impossible by construction, since `expected` is recomputed from the SAME `resolved.extents` the `View`'s own strides were built against. `max_flat_reduction_suffix_len`'s refactor from `reduction_is_fully_flat` is behavior-preserving by inspection (identical loop body; the bool became `len == reduction_dims.len()`) and re-confirmed by the full existing test suite staying green (446/446, no new failure). The kernel itself (`gemm_tile_neon`) is unmodified. No change to `Op`/`ScalarOp`/`IndexMap`, no change to `bind.rs`/`lower.rs` — every new symbol is `cpu.rs`-internal (`ConvGemmContext`, `ConvGemmTilePlan`, `conv_gemm_tile_plan`, `try_conv_gemm_assignment`, `axes_flat_chain`, `run_conv_gemm_tile`, `conv_gemm_row_block`, all `#[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]`, none `pub`) plus one new `instrument::Path::ConvTile` variant + `PATH_CONV_TILE` counter for path-kind visibility, mirroring `Path::DotFast`/`Path::WidthFast` exactly.

The residual gap's most likely source, not measured this session and named as the next diagnostic rather than guessed at: `width_fast`'s own 1040/20=52-invocation/image share of the forward pass (the FC/attention-shaped folds, unmodified by this row) now dominates the remaining wall time by elimination, since `conv_tile`'s own isolated micro-bench numbers above (12-276 µs per fold, ~0.85 ms summed across all 3 `Conv` folds at their real sizes) account for well under half of the 2.48 ms whole-model mean.

**Allocation budget.** Hot path (`run_conv_gemm_tile`/`conv_gemm_row_block`'s tile/outer/remainder loops): **zero** — code-read verified (every buffer is a caller-owned slice or a stack-resident `[[f32; TILE_COLS]; ROWS]`/`[f32; TILE_COLS]` array; no `Vec`/`Box`/`.collect()` anywhere in either function). Setup path (`conv_gemm_tile_plan`/`try_conv_gemm_assignment`, once per bound-op call = 3x/image for `Conv`): **exactly one** `Vec<u16>` (`n_axes`, capacity `<=` `leading_output_axes.len()`, e.g. 3 elements) — the failed M/N assignment attempt (`windowed` tried as `M` first) returns `None` during the `m_axis` search, BEFORE reaching the `n_axes` allocation, so only the successful attempt ever allocates; same setup-path cadence `run_reduce`'s own pre-existing `reduction_strides: Vec<i64>` already pays. **Caveat, named not papered over: neither number is measured via a tracking-allocator harness this session** — `instrument::AllocSiteGuard` exists in this crate for exactly this but requires a `#[global_allocator]` wrapper installed at the binary root, out of this row's bounded-fix budget; the zero-hot-path claim rests on code inspection plus the mechanism reasoning above, not an instrumented count, and is flagged unproven-by-instrumentation rather than asserted as measured.

- **A nested-odometer outer reduction (more than one outer axis) — NOT implemented, scoped out deliberately.** `conv_gemm_tile_plan` requires `reduction_dims.len() - inner_len == 1` (exactly one outer axis). Every one of `Conv`'s 3 real mnist folds has exactly one (`ci`); a hypothetical shape needing 2+ outer axes (e.g. a grouped conv with an extra un-flattened group axis) would correctly decline this gate and fall to `Generic`, not silently miscompute. Named as the honest next-widening step, not attempted, per this row's own bounded-fix budget.

**`docs/discipline.md` opt-sweep note (§11, applied where it binds — this is executor-internal hot-path code, not a sans-IO wire component, so most sans-IO-specific axes are N/A; the hot-path defaults still bind).** State machine: N/A (a straight-line tiled loop nest, not a protocol state machine). Bytes-first/borrowed views: DONE — every operand is a borrowed `&[f32]` slice, no owned intermediate. Zero-copy: DONE — no data movement beyond the NEON loads `gemm_tile_neon` already performs. Copy-over-clone: N/A (no cloning anywhere in the new code). SIMD: DONE — reuses `gemm_tile_neon`'s existing NEON `float32x4_t` accumulator tile unchanged. Stack-over-heap: DONE for the hot path (see allocation budget); setup path pays one small `Vec` per bound-op call, same as the file's existing convention. Branchless inner loop: PARTIAL — the tiled main loop is branch-free per iteration (no data-dependent branch inside `gemm_tile_neon`'s own `k`-loop), but the row/column-remainder dispatch (`match remaining { 1..=5 => ... }`) is a compile-time-resolved branch on a per-call, not per-element, boundary — same shape the existing dot tile already has. No dynamic dispatch: DONE — no `dyn`/`Box` anywhere in the new code. O(1) per token: N/A framing (this is a compute kernel, not a per-token wire op) — the domain-correct axis is O(1) per output element amortized over the tile, satisfied by construction (`gemm_tile_neon`'s own fixed-size accumulator).

## ROW 150 — instrument-first profile of the 2.479ms REFUTES ROW 149's own "by elimination" residual attribution (`width_fast`/`dot_fast` folds are near-zero, not dominant); the real residual is `elementwise` (Conv's own `window_materialize` im2col copy), and a bounded, mechanism-targeted tweak lands a MEASURED, reproducible win on it — whole-model criterion mean 2.4789ms -> 2.2991ms (-7.25%), inside/at the edge of host noise; NOT the 1.4ms burn-parity bar

Repo: `/Users/brianbruggeman/repos/slot-0/proxima-wt-neon`, branch `perf/residual-profile`, off `e0928ca` (ROW 149's own sealed HEAD). `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` pinned to a scratchpad dir for every command below. Host: Apple M1 Max, macOS, arm64. Build profile: `dev` for tests/clippy/mnist_diag, `release`/`bench` for the sealed bench — never mixed with correctness runs. Host loadout at every TIMING run: `pgrep -fl 'cargo|rustc'` showed no build process running (only `cdb-daemon`/`sccache`) at every check; `uptime` load average ran 11-32 throughout the session, the same "quiet at measurement, loaded moments earlier from other agents on this box" character ROW 145-149 all flagged — **MARKED LOADED**, not a quiet-box session; every number below is reported as a range/CoV, never a bare point estimate, exactly because of this.

### Step 1 — profile the 2.479ms, per-phase and per-fold-path, provenance-tagged

**Method.** `proxima-onnx/examples/mnist_diag.rs` (`mnist-diag` feature -> `proxima-tensor/instrument`) already carried a per-node-kind wall-time breakdown (`evaluate_quantized_with_scratch`'s own `DIAG evaluate_quantized node_kind=...` block, pre-existing, un-committed-since-ROW-139-era instrumentation) and a `BodyShape`-split (`elementwise_monomorphic`/`elementwise_generic`), but **two gaps blocked the task's own ask**: (1) no fast/slow-path split existed for the `Monomorphic` (`Unary`/`Binary`) elementwise bucket — only `Generic` had one — so it was impossible to tell whether Conv's own `window_materialize` multiply (`proxima-onnx/src/lower.rs:2320`, a `Binary` body) was hitting the vectorized width-copy or falling to the per-element gather loop; (2) `reduce_f32_dense`'s own timer summed ALL THREE reduce path kinds (`dot_fast`/`width_fast`/`conv_tile`) into one bucket, with only INVOCATION counts (not wall time) split by path — exactly the gap that let ROW 149 attribute the residual "by elimination" rather than measurement. Both gaps closed this session as new, `instrument`-gated, executor-internal counters (`ELEMENTWISE_LOOP_TICKS_MONOMORPHIC_FAST/SLOW`, `REDUCE_PATH_{DOT_FAST,WIDTH_FAST,CONV_TILE,GENERIC}_TICKS`), mirroring the file's own pre-existing `Generic`-split pattern exactly — no new public API, no new `Op`/`ScalarOp`/`IndexMap`.

**Cross-check that resolves ROW 149's ambiguity.** `PATH_DOT_FAST`=4/image and `PATH_CONV_TILE`=3/image (both from `instrument::totals()`'s pre-existing counters) match `run_reduce`'s own fold-count split EXACTLY (4+3=7=`node_kind=reduce_f32_dense`'s own count). `PATH_WIDTH_FAST`=52/image does **NOT** match any reduce fold — with the new per-path REDUCE ticks showing reduce's width tile fires **zero times**, the entire 52/image `PATH_WIDTH_FAST` count is `run_elementwise_range`'s OWN, textually-identical-but-semantically-unrelated `Path::WidthFast` (its affine-fast-path-vs-gather-loop classification, a different axis entirely — both functions reuse the same 4-variant `Path` enum, which is what let ROW 149 conflate them). **ROW 149's own sentence — "`width_fast`'s own 1040/20=52-invocation/image share of the forward pass (the FC/attention-shaped folds, unmodified by this row) now dominates the remaining wall time by elimination" — is REFUTED by direct measurement: that count is not reduce folds at all, and reduce's width tile contributes 0µs.** The real residual is `elementwise`, specifically `elementwise_monomorphic`'s 3 `window_materialize` calls (Conv's im2col copy), consistent with the task's own pre-registered lever (a).

**Mechanism, MEASURED not assumed.** `elementwise_monomorphic`'s own shape is `[n,c,oh,ow,kh,kw]` (`window_materialize`, `proxima-onnx/src/lower.rs:2320`); `run_elementwise_range`'s `split_innermost` treats only the LAST dim (`kw`=3) as the vectorized `inner_len`, leaving `kh`=3 (and `oy`,`ox`,`c`,`n`) in the ODOMETER outer loop — for the 3 real mnist Conv layers this is 39084 total outer positions, each computing only 3 elements. New `ELEMENTWISE_LOOP_TICKS_MONOMORPHIC_FAST/SLOW` split (added this session) shows **100% of the 117262 monomorphic elements take the FAST (affine width-copy, SIMD-eligible) path — zero slow/gather-loop elements** — refuting the a-priori hypothesis that the im2col copy was gather-bound; the cost is the fixed per-outer-position overhead (`unflatten_into` + `fill_running_offsets`, an O(rank)+O(operands) recompute) amortized over only 3 elements: measured 12.9-15.3 ns/element (BEFORE, `mnist_diag_before.log`, n=21, mean 13.71 ns/element) against this crate's own cited 0.38 ns/element pure-monomorphic figure (`cpu.rs:2159`'s doc) — a ~34-40x gap entirely attributable to per-call fixed cost, not bandwidth or gather.

### Step 2 — the tweak: block the second-to-last (`kh`) dim into the same call instead of the odometer, when the fast path is already engaged

**Design.** `Layout::offset_of` (`bind.rs:102`) is exactly linear in the coordinate (`base + Σ coordinate[d]*stride[d]`), so for ANY dim `d`, `offset_of(coord with d bumped by h) == offset_of(coord) + h*stride(d)` — exact, not approximate, and holds for every operand `run_elementwise_range`'s fast path admits (fast_path already requires every referenced operand to be gather-free, `body_shape_is_affine_fast_path`/`operand_is_affine`, so no `Lookup` overlay is ever in scope here). `run_elementwise_range` (`cpu.rs`) gains: a loop-invariant `block_dim`/`block_extent`/`block_strides` computed once per call (the dim immediately outside `inner_len`, e.g. `kh`), and — inside the main loop, converted from a `for` to a `while` so a block can consume more than one position — a new branch that fires only when `fast_path` holds, `block_extent > 1`, the current position starts a fresh sweep of `block_dim` (its own coordinate is 0), and a full `block_extent`-long run still fits before `outer_end` (so a parallel-chunk boundary mid-sweep, or an unaligned `outer_start`, transparently falls through to the unchanged per-position path — verified by construction, not tested against every chunk boundary explicitly). Inside a block: ONE `unflatten_into`+`fill_running_offsets` call, then `block_extent - 1` cheap `running[i] += block_strides[i]` increments replacing the recompute, calling `elementwise_width_fast` once per sub-position exactly as before (kernel call count UNCHANGED — only the odometer bookkeeping shrinks). Falls straight through to the existing single-position code whenever `block_extent <= 1` (any op whose rank leaves nothing to merge) — zero behavior change for every other shape in the crate.

**Correctness reasoning.** The block loop computes the IDENTICAL sequence of `running` offsets the unblocked loop would have computed (by `Layout::offset_of`'s own linearity, proven above, not empirically fuzzed) — every `elementwise_width_fast` call receives the same `running`/`out_slice` it would have under the old code, so output is bit-identical by construction. Verified: 446/446 `proxima-tensor` tests green (unchanged N from ROW 149), including every existing `neon_tile_full_output`/elementwise fixture; MNIST accuracy bit-identical at 0.9900 (990/1000) both before and after.

**No new `Op`/`ScalarOp`/`IndexMap`, no new public type.** Every new symbol (`block_dim`, `block_extent`, `block_strides`, `ELEMENTWISE_LOOP_TICKS_MONOMORPHIC_FAST/SLOW`, `REDUCE_PATH_*_TICKS`, `record_reduce_path_ticks`) is `cpu.rs`/`instrument.rs`-internal, `instrument`-gated where diagnostic, none `pub` outside the crate's existing `instrument` module surface.

**Allocation budget.** Hot path (the block/single-position loops themselves): **zero** — `block_strides` is one `Vec<i64>` allocated ONCE per `run_elementwise_range` call (same setup-path cadence as the pre-existing `strides`/`running` Vecs this function already allocates), never inside the position loop. Not measured via a tracking-allocator harness this session (same caveat ROW 149 flagged for its own allocation claim) — code-inspection-verified, not instrumented-counted.
